Aviation NDT training in San Antonio: the short answer

Aviation NDT training in San Antonio means preparing technicians for eddy current, fluorescent penetrant, ultrasonic and radiographic work on engines and airframes at Port San Antonio, the JBSA bases and the Part 145 shops around them. Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training live online or onsite at your facility, led by an ASNT Level III. Most prime contractors and MROs certify under NAS 410, so our training fits as theory foundation, for non-NAS suppliers, and as Level III support.

That last sentence matters more in San Antonio than almost anywhere else in Texas, so this page is written to be honest about it. If your shop certifies under NAS 410 (or its European equivalent, EN 4179), your Responsible Level 3 and your written practice decide what training counts. If you are a machine shop, a ground-support or tooling supplier, a non-destructive testing contractor that also works industrial jobs, or a technician building method knowledge before an aviation employer certifies you, SNT-TC-1A-based training is a direct fit. The sections below explain which is which, so you can decide before you ask for a quote.

Request a San Antonio aviation NDT training quote or read on.

Aviation NDT work in San Antonio

San Antonio's aviation NDT demand is concentrated, unusually, on one runway. Kelly Field, the industrial airport at Port San Antonio on the site of the former Kelly Air Force Base, shares its runway with Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland. Around it sit some of the largest aircraft and engine maintenance operations in the country. Port San Antonio lists Boeing, Lockheed Martin, StandardAero and Chromalloy among its aerospace employers, and Boeing describes its Port San Antonio site as its largest aircraft modernisation complex. StandardAero runs engine maintenance and overhaul there, and the port advertises one of the country's largest arrays of jet engine test cells south of the runway. These names are context for where the work is; Atlantis has no relationship with any of them and does not claim one.

What that concentration means for an NDT technician is a very specific mix of work:

  • Engine overhaul. Disks, blades, vanes, cases and shafts come apart, get cleaned, and are inspected against OEM manual limits. Fluorescent penetrant (PT) lines and eddy current (ET) on bolt holes and blade roots dominate; UT and immersion techniques cover rotating parts where the manual calls for them.
  • Airframe heavy maintenance and modernisation. Military transport and tanker-class aircraft come through for programmed depot maintenance and structural modification. That brings ET on fastener holes and lap joints, low-frequency ET for second-layer cracking, UT thickness and corrosion mapping, bond testing on bonded structure, and film or digital radiography on assemblies that cannot be opened.
  • Component and accessory shops. Landing gear, wheels and brakes, actuators and castings: MT on high-strength steel gear components, ET on wheel bead seats, PT on aluminium and titanium parts.
  • Military base maintenance. JBSA-Lackland and JBSA-Randolph host flying units and training wings. Uniformed NDI technicians are trained and certified inside the military system, not by commercial schools; many of them move into the civilian shops when they separate, which is why veteran transition is a large part of the San Antonio picture.

Outside aviation, the same metro has a large truck assembly plant, energy work tied to the Eagle Ford shale to the south, and the usual fabrication and construction inspection load of a major Texas city. Technicians here often hold industrial SNT-TC-1A certifications alongside, or before, an aviation certification. Our general NDT training in San Antonio page covers that industrial side; this page stays with aviation.

Methods used in San Antonio aviation work, and the standards behind them

MethodAviation application in San AntonioCode / standard (context)
ET (eddy current)Bolt-hole and fastener-hole inspection on airframes, blade-root and disk slot inspection in engine overhaul, wheel bead seats, conductivity checks on heat-damaged aluminiumOEM NDT manuals, aircraft structural repair and NDT manuals, ASTM E1004 (conductivity), NAS 410 for personnel
PT (fluorescent penetrant)Engine hot-section and rotating parts, aluminium and titanium airframe fittings, castingsASTM E1417, AMS 2644 materials, OEM specs, NAS 410 for personnel
MT (magnetic particle)Landing gear, high-strength steel shafts and fittings, ground-support equipmentASTM E1444, OEM specs
UT (ultrasonic)Thickness and corrosion mapping on skins, bond and disbond checks, forging and rotating-part immersion inspectionOEM manuals, ASTM E2375 (wrought products), customer specs
PAUTCorrosion mapping and composite or bonded-structure scanning where the OEM approves itOEM-approved procedures
RT / DRCastings, honeycomb water ingress, assemblies that cannot be disassembled; digital radiography increasingly replacing filmASTM E1742, ASTM E2698 (DR), state radiation rules for any source or X-ray use
VTBorescope inspection of engines, general visual inspection that triggers every other methodOEM manuals, FAA maintenance requirements
Bond testing (context)Composite and bonded-metal structureOEM procedures; often treated as its own qualification within NAS 410 programmes

Atlantis trains the SNT-TC-1A method courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. We do not offer bond testing, NAS 410 certification or OEM-specific engine training. If your role is ET-heavy, start with the eddy current Level II course. For engine shops, the penetrant Level II course is usually first.

Which certification scheme San Antonio aviation employers expect

This is the question most San Antonio searchers are really asking. The table answers it honestly.

SchemeWho in San Antonio typically requires itDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
NAS 410 / EN 4179Aerospace primes, large MROs and engine shops, and suppliers to them. Certification is issued by the employer under its own written practice, with a Responsible Level 3Partly. Our classroom content builds the method theory, but your employer decides whether it counts toward NAS 410 hours. We do not certify to NAS 410. See NAS 410 certification requirements
ASNT SNT-TC-1ANon-aerospace suppliers, machine and fabrication shops, ground-support and tooling makers, industrial NDT contractors, some smaller repair stations whose customers accept itYes. This is the scheme we train to, including Level III exam preparation
Military NDI programmesUniformed NDI technicians on the JBSA basesNo. The military trains its own; we can help veterans map that experience onto an SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 written practice
FAA Part 145 repair-station rulesEvery certificated repair station. Part 145 governs the station, its manuals and its training programme; it does not itself issue NDT certificationsContext only. The station's manual will name the personnel standard it uses (often NAS 410)
ASNT ACCP / CP-189Rare in aviation; some customers ask for ACCPTheory foundation only

So, if you are a technician hoping to join a large San Antonio MRO: your employer will certify you under NAS 410. What you can do beforehand is learn the methods properly, understand the physics and the paperwork, and arrive ready. If you are an employer whose customers accept SNT-TC-1A, we can train, examine through your Level III, and help write the written practice that ties it together.

The SNT-TC-1A path in San Antonio, step by step

  1. Your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. Your company's written practice sets the training, experience and examination rules. If you do not have one, see written practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. Method theory, equipment, techniques, codes and acceptance criteria, delivered live online or onsite. Required hours depend on method and level; we link the training requirements matrix rather than quote figures, because your written practice may set them higher.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged under a certified technician, on real aviation parts and procedures.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. Administered by a Level III. In aviation the specific exam should use your shop's procedures and the OEM manual references your technicians actually work to.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, renewed annually.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies, not the trainer. Recertification follows the interval in your written practice.

For the employer-side detail, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing, base access and other San Antonio requirements

Texas is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography in Texas, whether with isotopes or X-ray, is regulated by the Texas Department of State Health Services radiation control programme, and radiographers and radiographer trainees must meet the state's certification and training rules before they work. If your San Antonio shop runs a cabinet X-ray or digital radiography system, the registration and safety requirements still apply; check the current rules with the department before planning RT training. Atlantis teaches radiographic interpretation and technique under SNT-TC-1A; we do not issue state radiation safety credentials.

Work on JBSA installations requires base access, usually arranged through the employer and its contract, and some programmes require a security clearance. Work inside Port San Antonio facilities follows each tenant's own access and badging rules. None of this is part of NDT training, but it affects how quickly a newly trained technician can start.

How Atlantis delivers aviation NDT training to San Antonio

We have no training centre in San Antonio or anywhere else, and we will not pretend to. There are three ways we deliver:

  • Live online. Instructor-led classroom sessions in real time, suited to individuals and to shops that cannot release a whole shift. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. A Level III-led course at your San Antonio shop, on your equipment and your reference standards, using your procedures. For engine and component shops this is almost always the better model, because the practical work happens on the parts and blocks your technicians will see.
  • Blended. Theory live online, then a short onsite block for practicals and examinations.

We schedule around production rather than the other way round: depot induction schedules, engine shop surges and contract milestones drive aviation workload, and a cohort can be split across shifts. Ask about onsite training for your San Antonio crew. Group and onsite quotes come back within one business day; see corporate NDT training for how cohorts work.

Level III services and written practices for San Antonio shops

Smaller aviation-adjacent shops often lack an in-house Level III. Atlantis provides ASNT Level III support under SNT-TC-1A: writing or reviewing the written practice, preparing and administering examinations, reviewing procedures and technique sheets, and audit preparation when a customer comes to look. If your customer demands NAS 410, we can explain the gap between your current SNT-TC-1A programme and NAS 410 requirements, but the NAS 410 Responsible Level 3 role must be filled under that standard. For the local consulting side, see NDT consulting in San Antonio, or book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments, one of which is an aircraft hangar. It is useful for learning probe handling, scan patterns and indication recognition before touching a real part, and for revising between sessions. It is practice only: it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that your written practice requires. San Antonio users can also start from Practical NDT for San Antonio.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Level III oversight covers course content, examinations and the written-practice side of every programme we run.

Veterans moving from military NDI into San Antonio shops

San Antonio's military aviation base produces a steady flow of trained NDI technicians into civilian work. Military NDI experience is real experience, but civilian certification is still issued by the civilian employer under its written practice. In practice that means documenting your training and hours, sitting the employer's examinations, and sometimes filling theory gaps. Our guide for veterans transitioning into NDT covers the process. On funding, be careful: GI Bill and WIOA money generally goes only to approved schools and programmes, and Atlantis does not claim that approval. The usual route for our courses is employer-paid training.

Frequently asked questions about aviation NDT training in San Antonio

Where can I get aviation NDT training in San Antonio?

The main routes are an employer's own NAS 410 programme at a San Antonio MRO or engine shop, a local school such as those listed above, or SNT-TC-1A-based training from Atlantis delivered live online or onsite at your employer's facility. Which is right depends on whether your target employer certifies under NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by San Antonio aerospace employers?

Many aerospace primes and MROs certify under NAS 410, not SNT-TC-1A. Some suppliers, non-aerospace shops and smaller repair stations work to SNT-TC-1A. Classroom training under SNT-TC-1A can still build the theory your NAS 410 employer expects, but only your employer can say whether the hours count.

Do I need NAS 410 to work at Port San Antonio?

For NDT roles at the large aerospace tenants, expect to be certified under NAS 410 by the employer after you are hired. You do not need to hold it beforehand; employers train new hires. Read NAS 410 certification requirements for the structure.

Which NDT method should I learn first for aviation work?

Penetrant is the most common starting method in engine shops, and eddy current is the signature airframe method. Many San Antonio technicians start on a penetrant line and add ET and UT as they progress.

How long does aviation NDT training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A, it depends on the method, the level and your written practice: formal classroom hours plus logged on-the-job experience. See the training requirements matrix. NAS 410 sets its own requirements, which your employer applies.

Can I take aviation NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, the classroom portion can be taken live online. Practical examinations must be done on real specimens, usually at your employer's facility.

What does aviation NDT training cost in San Antonio?

We quote on request. Cost depends on the methods and levels, the number of trainees, live online versus onsite delivery, and whether examinations and written-practice work are included. Onsite and cohort quotes come back within one business day.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes. Texas regulates industrial radiography through the Department of State Health Services, and radiographers must meet state certification and training rules. NDT training alone does not license you to operate a source.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for aviation NDT training?

Generally only at approved schools and programmes. Atlantis does not claim that approval, so for our courses the normal route is employer sponsorship. Check with the VA or Workforce Solutions Alamo for approved local options.

Does Atlantis offer NAS 410 or bond testing training?

No. We train to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III preparation. NAS 410 and bond testing are mentioned here only as context.

Can you train our San Antonio repair station onsite?

Yes, if SNT-TC-1A fits your programme. We deliver at your facility on your equipment and procedures. Ask about onsite training for your San Antonio shop.

What do aviation NDT technicians earn in San Antonio?

We do not publish salary figures for individual cities. See our NDT salary guide for published ranges and sources.

Next steps

Technicians can prepare for an aviation NDT career with our NDT training courses, practise with Practical NDT, and revise with UT Level II practice questions. Employers can request a quote for a San Antonio aviation cohort, and Level III candidates can look at ASNT Level III training.
